description: The dashboard served by the daemon on loopback. It may read the daemon's state, open web links, drag the window, fill the menu bar and badge, set the global hotkey and show and withdraw OS notifications, and install a signed app update when the user clicks for it or chose Update automatically (F20, ADR-042), and for a feedback report put an image on the clipboard, capture its own page read an image file the user just dropped on the window, read a file of at most 10 MB the user just dropped on an open chat (to attach it as the Attach button would), read a .md or .txt file the user just dropped on the window as the brief of New project from a template, set its own zoom (Appearance → Interface size), and open the system's folder chooser for New project (it returns the path the user picked), and open Mail in its own window: the installed Caprock Mail preview on macOS, else a second window of this app on the daemon's /?mail=1, and open, place, hide and close the web page a browser tab shows, in a window of its own laid over the tab (the in-app browser, ADR-075), and add a line to the app's own log on this machine (app.log in the data directory) when its crash screen or its start-up watchdog shows, and on macOS listen to the microphone while the user holds or clicks the chat's microphone button, recognised on this Mac only (no audio or text leaves it), the words coming back to this page alone (ADR-102); on Windows and Linux the same through whisper.cpp in the app, and in Settings → Voice input read the voice model's state, download it from huggingface.co on the user's click (its SHA-256 checked against hashes built into the app), cancel that download, delete the model and show it in the file manager (ADR-103). Nothing else that starts processes or touches files: launching that one installed app is the only process, the hotkey choice, that verified update and those bounded log lines and the voice model the user downloads are the only writes.
